Hi, Thu,
1. It is an ON / OFF dialing function to activate those functions as
described in the datasheet.
There is certain part on the PCB board to enable / disable it.

2. A similar example is
*https://www.lantronix.com/products/sgetf-series-2/#product-specifications
<https://www.lantronix.com/products/sgetf-series-2/#product-specifications>*
6-Position Switch
SW1: Remote Fiber Fault Detect (Down=Enabled)
SW2: Symmetric Pause
SW3: Asymmetric Pause
SW4: Transparent Link Pass Through (UP=Enabled)
SW5: Fiber Auto-Negotiation (Down=Enabled)
SW6: Loopback (Down=Enabled)


*And this model
https://www.level1.com/level1_en/gvt-2000-rj-45-to-sfp-gigabit-ethernet-media-converter-540678
<https://www.level1.com/level1_en/gvt-2000-rj-45-to-sfp-gigabit-ethernet-media-converter-540678>*
3. Most media converters are unmanaged, DIP features are the primary (and
sometimes only) way to configure the device.
Like those features mentioned above.

Thank you.
